tweets.text:
My last post on “How to make ₦1M with AI Customer Chatbots” blew up…

So let me show you another unconventional client acquisition method that you can use to hit this target that most people don’t even know exists.

This one is not the normal “send cold emails” or “DM random businesses.”

No.
This is more strategic.
More targeted.
And honestly… this is how I would hunt clients if I was desperate to close deals fast.

Read this to the end👇👇

1. Instagram Targeting (But Not the Way Everybody Does It)

Most people go to Instagram and look for “any business” they can message.
That’s why they don’t get replies.
Here’s how I do it:

👉 Pick a niche — Hair Vendors, SPAs, Restaurants, Hotels, or Skincare brands.
👉 Search for brands with 50k+ followers (not the small ones).
👉 These ones are your ideal clients because their DM volume is crazy in December.
👉 Follow them.
👉 Study their videos, their comments, their customer flow.
You are not pitching blindly.
You are studying their operation so your pitch is relevant.
Then you send your outreach.

Now here is what I do and has constantly work for me 

Voice notes work 10x better than text.
But don’t send a 2-minute motivational talk.

Be strategic and short:
“Hey, I noticed you get a lot of enquiries. I built an AI customer support that replies instantly and reduces missed sales. If you want a quick demo, I can show you.”
People open voice notes out of curiosity.
That's your advantage.

2. The Hidden Goldmine: Facebook Ads Library

This one is what most people don’t know about.

Go to Facebook Ads Library.
Search the same niche.
You will see:

Businesses currently running ads

Their landing pages

Their CTA

Where they are driving traffic

What they are promoting this season

If a business is running ads right now, two things are already confirmed:

✔ They want more customers
✔ They have money to spend

Those are the people you should pitch your chatbot to.
And here’s the sweet part…

When you open their landing page, you already know how their sales process works.
So you can pitch with incredible accuracy:

“Hey, I saw your December promo. You’re probably getting a lot of enquiries. I built an AI agent that replies instantly so you don’t lose sales while running ads.”

Some of you only know how to build the chatbot…
But you don’t know how to sell it.
This strategy alone can get you:

Hot leads

Faster replies

Higher closing rates

Because you're pitching to people who already have demand, not people who are “managing life.”

I might make a full video breakdown of this strategy if you want.

Let me know.

But I hope you got value from this.
Don’t just build  be strategic.
December is the perfect month to close deals if you know where to look.
Go execute.

tweets.text:
Why customers buy from you, and why they don’t?

The answer is hidden in the 5A’s.

Here are more details about them:

1. Aware

They’ve heard of you.
No awareness = no chance.
Branding, SEO, ads, and PR build this.

2. Appeal

They’re intrigued.
Boring brands die fast.
Emotion, design, story - all make you stand out.

3. Ask

They seek more info.
If you’re invisible, you’re irrelevant.
Reviews, social proof, and content matter here.

4. Act

They buy, sign up, or call.
Confused users don’t convert.
Make it simple, frictionless, and obvious.

5. Advocate

They promote you.
Referrals beat any ad campaign.
Delight them so much they brag to friends.

Your goal?

Move people from Aware to Advocate.

And if your funnel leaks, plug it fast.

P.S. Which “A” needs the most work in your business?

tweets.text:
This Is How You Can Build Digital Skills Fast In Nigeria (Thread)
👇👇
1/
Let’s be honest…
The economy is hard.
Jobs are scarce.
But digital skills is still the FASTEST way to make money locally or globally.
Here is a simple roadmap to learn any digital skill fast.
No long story.
👇

2/
🎯 Pick a skill that actually pays
Don’t learn “everything.”
Choose just one from this list:
Data analysis
UI/UX
Graphic design
Video editing
Copywriting
Social media mgmt
Web dev
Digital marketing
AI tools / automation
Pick ONE. Focus on it.

3/
📱 Use your phone first
You don’t need a laptop to begin.
Most beginners delay because of equipment.
Start with your phone.
You can learn, practice, edit videos, design graphics, write copy - all from your phone.
Your phone is a machine. Use it.

4/
📚 Free learning platforms that ACTUALLY work
Here are the top free places Nigerians use to learn quickly:
YouTube (start with beginners playlists)
Coursera (Financial aid available)
Google Digital Skills Africa
Udemy (₦3k sales often)
LinkedIn Learning (free month)
FreeCodeCamp (for coding)

No excuses!

5/
🧪 Learn → Practice → Post your work
The fastest way to grow is to document your journey.
Learned design? Post your designs.
Learned coding? Share mini projects.
Learning video editing? Post before/after edits.
Post on X, LinkedIn, Tiktok, everywhere you can.
Consistency makes people notice you.

6/
📂 Build a simple portfolio (in 7 days)
Don’t overthink it.
Just gather:
3–5 sample works
A short bio
Your contact
Tools you use

Host it on:
👉 Notion
👉 Canva
👉 Google Drive
👉 GitHub (for coders)
Nobody cares about fancy. Just show proof. Show working.

7/
🤝 Start working before you feel “ready”
Message small businesses:
“Hi, I noticed your page/website/design/copy can be better. I can help you improve it with [your skill]. Here are my samples.”
Many people have landed jobs this way.
Start with low-cost jobs → build track record → raise prices.

8/
💼 Go global early
Nigeria is competitive.
The world pays better.
Create accounts on:
Upwork
Fiverr
Contra
LinkedIn
Outlier (Very good for remote jobs)
Your first goal: Get 1 international client.
It changes everything.

9/
⚡ Use AI to learn faster
AI won’t replace you if you learn to use it.
Use tools like:
ChatGPT
Canva AI
CapCut AI
Notion AI
Mixo AI (landing pages)
Descript (audio/video edits)
AI = speed + quality, if you know how to use it.

10/
🔋 Stay on it for 30 days
30 days can change your skill level drastically.
Do this daily:
1 hour of learning
1 hour of practicing
20 minutes of posting your work
Small actions → big results.

11/
💰 Bonus: High-demand skills right now
If you want FAST opportunities, focus on:
Social media management
Video editing
Canva design
Facebook ads
UI/UX
Customer support (remote)
Virtual assistant
Data entry + AI tools
These are easy to learn & easy to monetize.

12/
🔥 Final take:
You don’t need connections.
You don’t need a laptop.
You don’t need money to start.
You only need discipline + consistency for 30 days.
Digital skills can change your income, location, and you life - faster than anything else.

tweets.text:
I’m obsessed with CRE marketing materials and spent a ton of time designing our templates.  I review every single package. 

I also think OM’s have almost no impact on the sale price,  lease price or even the number of offers. 

The most effective marketing tools are accurate underwriting, pricing and exposure to the right people.  

You can do all that on a powerpoint with comic sans font (please don’t. Papyrus isn’t allowed either). 

So why do we spend so much time and money on good marketing materials and professional photos and drones?  Because it’s a reflection of our team and how we want to be perceived. 

But I’m sincere when I say, it doesn’t matter for client results. 

Agents spend way too much time worrying about looks and not enough time on accuracy and how they will actually market and to whom.  

If you aren’t getting activity it’s not because you need a third aerial and a fresh marketing package.

It’s either not priced right, doesn’t have accurate info, or isn’t in front of the right people.

Every time I'm at a YC event, I get asked how to do GTM.

My answer is always the same - here are the bullet points:

1. build your lead lists, use tools like Crustdata or Apollo  
2. don't use AI to create the outbound email - make it as concise as possible  
3. take a look at deliverability metrics - iterate email every day - make it more and more punchy  
4. separately, use LI Sales Nav to write 2 sentence outreach to people - preferably with warm connection (common university, etc)
5. Post on LinkedIn everyday  
6. invest in SEO  

spend 80% of your time on the above and you will breakthrough and get demos

Every founder who followed this advice with enough discipline saw results.

tweets.text:
The death of the average.

We are currently witnessing the total collapse of the marginal cost of creation. Copywriting, design, video editing - skills that previously commanded a premium due to the barrier of technical execution are being democratised to the point of irrelevance.

Most marketers view this through the lens of efficiency. They see a tool that allows them to produce 10x the output for 1/10th of the cost.

When the supply of "good enough" content becomes infinite, the economic value of that content plummets to zero. We are entering an era of infinite noise. If you think it is hard to capture attention now, wait until the internet is flooded with billions of synthetically generated articles, tweets, and videos every single day.

(Which is already happening, just not at the quality and volume that it will in 6, 12 months from now)

In this environment, pure volume is no longer a valid strategy. You cannot out-publish a server farm.

The alpha in modern marketing is shifting entirely from production to provenance.

[1] The Trust Premium

As the internet becomes increasingly synthetic, we will see a massive flight to safety. "Is this real?" will become the single most important buying criterion.

We are moving away from algorithm-optimisation and back towards human-optimisation. Personal brands, founders-led sales, and verified human voices will command an exorbitant premium.

The faceless corporate brand is dead. If a consumer cannot verify the human source behind the message, they will subconsciously label it as "spam".

[2] High-Friction Marketing

For the last decade, the goal was "low friction". SEO, programmatic ads, automated email sequences.

As AI cannibalises these low-friction channels, - bots clicking on ads served by bots on sites written by bots - the smart money will move to high-friction channels.

Live events. Physical mail. Handshakes. Closed-door dinners.

The harder it is to scale, the more valuable it becomes. You prove your value by doing things that cannot be automated.

[3] Taste as a Moat

Large Language Models function by predicting the next most likely token. By definition, they regress to the mean. They give you the average of the entire internet.

If you use AI to guide your strategy, you are opting for mediocrity at scale.

"Taste" - the human ability to curate, to select the outlier, to understand nuance and subtext - becomes the only defensible moat.

The future of marketing is about who has the taste to know what *not* to create.

Paradoxically, the more artificial the world becomes, the higher the premium on being undeniably human.

tweets.text:
My Social Media Manager left for NYSC camp, so I needed a new one ASAP.

I didn’t want to post it publicly because that’s the fastest way to attract the wrong candidates and clog my inbox with chaos.

Then I remembered a girl who reached out weeks ago. She had just finished her virtual assistant training and asked if I had any tasks she could practice with. 

I gave her a small research task on my ICP. She delivered well.

So I reached out again and asked if she was available to handle my social media. She had never done it before, but she was willing to learn. 

Created an SOP for her. One week in. She’s doing great. Small mistakes, but she’s making progress.

If you’re a beginner in remote work, start by reaching out. Offer value. Ask if someone needs help. 

If she didn’t send that message, I wouldn’t have remembered her. I wouldn’t have reached out. This is how beginners get opportunities. This is how you get noticed.
